title: The 5 Heaviest Meteorites Ever Found, Ranked (#1 Never Moved)

scenes.text: The five heaviest meteorites ever found. Number one is still lying exactly where it fell.
Number five: Armanty, in China. About twenty-eight tonnes of metal from space.
scenes.label: Armanty · 28 tonnes

scenes.text: Number four: El Chaco, in Argentina. Twenty-eight point eight tonnes, one of several giants in one crater field.
scenes.label: El Chaco · 28.8 tonnes

scenes.text: Number three: Gancedo, from the same Argentine field. Thirty point eight tonnes.
scenes.label: Gancedo · 30.8 tonnes

scenes.text: Number two: the Cape York meteorite, found in Greenland. Thirty point nine tonnes, now in a New York museum.
scenes.label: Cape York · 30.9 tonnes

scenes.text: Number one: Hoba, in Namibia. Over sixty tonnes, found in 1920 when a plough hit it. It has never been moved.
scenes.label: Hoba · 60+ tonnes

description:
The five heaviest meteorites ever found, ranked by mass.
Number one weighs over 60 tonnes, twice as much as number two, and it has never been moved from where it landed.
Which of these would you most want to see in person?
first_comment: Which would you put at number one? And what should we rank next?
